Findings converge on the date-derived branch of Booking.state
findings.why_it_matters: `Booking.state` gives an unrecognized status an answer from its dates and a known status an answer from its name. Findings 2, 3, and 4 all come from the gap between those two answers. A member added later stops reading dates (Finding 2). An unknown late-cancel variant gets the opposite answer from the known `LateCancelled` (Finding 3). An unknown status the caller asked for by name can be removed by the exclusions, because only an unknown status can come out "cancelled" from a date (Finding 4). None of the three would remain if an unknown status always got the same answer a member gets. Does this point to a problem with the date-derived branch that should be re-evaluated, rather than patched finding by finding? The re-evaluation includes whether the branch is needed at all, and whether these failures are limitations to accept and document.
findings.recommended: B: Keep the date-derived branch and address Findings 2, 3, and 4 individually.
findings.chosen: B: Keep the date-derived branch and address Findings 2, 3, and 4 individually.

findings.title: Adding the enum member the WARNING asks for silently changes booking behavior
findings.why_it_matters: `Booking.state` names two members and sends every other `BookingStatus` member to "active". The date rule runs only for non-members. Suppose OTF adds "No Show" and a maintainer follows the WARNING by adding `NO_SHOW = "No Show"`. From that release, a record with `cancelledDate` set flips from "cancelled" to "active". `book_class` then raises `AlreadyBookedError` where it used to rebook, and `exclude_cancelled` keeps a record it used to remove. No test fails. D4 says "every other member is active", but that describes today's members and does not address the flip at the release.
findings.recommended: A: Add a parametrized test over `list(BookingStatus)` with an explicit expected state for each member, so a new member fails until someone decides.
findings.chosen: A: Add a parametrized test over `list(BookingStatus)` with an explicit expected state for each member, so a new member fails until someone decides.

findings.title: An unrecognized late-cancel variant gets the opposite treatment from the known LateCancelled
findings.why_it_matters: The known `LateCancelled` is deliberately "active": it blocks rebooking and stays in `get_bookings`. The captured data shows late-cancelled records carry `cancelledDate`. A respelled or new variant, such as `"Late cancelled"`, carries the same date, so it resolves to "cancelled": hidden by default and rebookable. On those 2 of 49 captured records, the date rule disagrees with the known mapping, so the ledger's note that the `LateCancelled` oddity "is unrelated to unknown values" is not accurate. `book_class` would then attempt a rebooking the server may refuse, and that refusal may surface as an unmapped error rather than `AlreadyBookedError`.
findings.recommended: C: Accept as a known limitation: an unrecognized late-cancel variant that carries `cancelledDate` reads as cancelled, unlike the known `LateCancelled`.
findings.chosen: C: Accept as a known limitation: an unrecognized late-cancel variant that carries `cancelledDate` reads as cancelled, unlike the known `LateCancelled`.
findings.choice_reason: lets fix finding 5, accept the other ones

findings.title: get_bookings with an unknown cancel-style status returns an empty list by default
findings.why_it_matters: D3 widened `status` so a value read from a response can be passed back in. If the caller passes `status="No Show"` and those records carry `cancelledDate`, they all resolve to "cancelled", and the default `exclude_cancelled=True` removes everything the caller asked for, with no signal. The existing guard turns the exclusion off only for `status == BookingStatus.Cancelled`. The same silent emptiness already exists on the default branch for known statuses: `status=BookingStatus.CheckedIn` with default flags and `status=[BookingStatus.Cancelled]` both strip what was requested. This input is new; the shape of the problem is not.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: `get_bookings(status=<unknown>)` with default flags drops records that carry the matching date, as it already does for `status=CheckedIn`.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: `get_bookings(status=<unknown>)` with default flags drops records that carry the matching date, as it already does for `status=CheckedIn`.
findings.choice_reason: lets fix finding 5, accept the other ones

findings.title: A false AlreadyBookedError on an inferred state gives no clue it was inferred
findings.why_it_matters: D4 accepted that a cancel-flavored status with no date is wrongly refused. It did not address that the refusal looks identical to a real one. `book_class` raises the same message whether the status is a known `Booked` or an unknown string inferred "active" from two null dates. The only related log line is the once-per-process WARNING from parse time, which may be hours old and says nothing about control flow.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a false refusal on an inferred state reads like a real one, and the bookings guide documents the case and the workaround.
findings.chosen: A: Add the booking's status to the `AlreadyBookedError` message in `book_class`.
findings.choice_reason: lets fix finding 5, accept the other ones

findings.title: The BREAKING CHANGE footer understates the break surface, and only the PR body reaches the changelog
findings.why_it_matters: release-please publishes the footer as the changelog's breaking-change text. The footer names only `.value`. These also break: any other enum attribute or method on the raw value (`.name`, which the challenges guide itself mentions, and the public `BookingStatus.priority()`, which a raw string lacks); `ClassFilter(class_type="typo")` no longer raises `KeyError`; and `ClassFilter.class_type`'s declared type now includes raw strings. Also, this repo squash-merges with `squash_merge_commit_title=PR_TITLE` and `squash_merge_commit_message=PR_BODY`, so the commit on `main` that release-please reads is built from the PR, not from e80624f. A footer that exists only on the local commit never reaches the changelog, and neither do the `Closes` lines.
findings.chosen: Replace the footer on the local commit (the branch has no upstream, so amending is safe) and put the same footer and the four `Closes` lines in the PR body when the PR is created, since that is what lands on `main`:

findings.title: ClassFilter.class_type does not have one stable stored shape
findings.why_it_matters: The field is declared with four arms, `list[ClassType] | list[str] | ClassType | str | None`, but `_normalize_class_types` always returns a list, so construction never reaches the scalar arms. The element type also changes with the input. A probe on this commit shows `[ClassType.ORANGE_60]` stores a `ClassType`, while `[ClassType.ORANGE_60, "HYROX_75"]` matches only `list[str]` and downcasts the known member to a plain `str`. Matching is unaffected because `filter_classes` compares through `class_type_key`.
findings.chosen: Side B: Declare one arm, Sequence[ClassType | str] | None

findings.title: Booking.state exists only on the v1 model
findings.why_it_matters: `Booking.state` is a new documented property with a three-value `Literal`. `BookingV2` is built as a compatibility facade for `Booking`, with `status`, `ends_at`, and `id_value`-style shims, but it has no `state`. Code written over `Booking | BookingV2` can use `.status` on both and `.state` only on v1. The documented `Literal` also commits to the `LateCancelled`-is-active quirk as a return value. The Build section does acknowledge `state` as the one new property to keep stable (design.md:223), so this is a known cost and not an accident; the open question is the asymmetry.
findings.chosen: Side A: Leave state on v1 only until v1 is retired

findings.title: A known lengthless class type logs louder than an unrecognized one
findings.why_it_matters: `get_end_time` logs a WARNING on every read for `OTHER` and now only DEBUG for an unrecognized type. `ends_at` is a property read repeatedly, so a long-running poller over `OTHER` classes keeps a flood of the kind D5 set out to remove. This is existing behavior on the default branch, and the Build section keeps it on purpose because D6 says `OTHER` is unchanged.
findings.chosen: Side B: Lower the OTHER arm to DEBUG

findings.title: The internal status of the new names rests on their absence from __all__
findings.why_it_matters: `OpenClassType`, `OpenBookingStatus`, `OpenStudioStatus`, `OpenEquipmentType`, `class_type_key`, `normalize_to`, `reported_values`, `minutes_from_class_type_name`, and `known_class_type_or_raw` are all importable, non-underscore names. None of them is exported from a package `__init__`, which matches D7, but nothing else tells a consumer they are internal. The critic reads the repo as having a no-underscore convention. The house coding-style rule does allow `_` when the code is part of a published library with a stable API contract, which this one is.
findings.chosen: Side A: Leave it
